senses.gloss:
Śākhā in the Rigveda^1 and later^2 denotes the ‘branch’ of a
tree. Vayā is more often used in this sense in the Rigveda.
1) i. 8, 8; vii. 43, 1; x. 94, 3.
2) Av. iii. 6, 8; x. 7, 21; xi. 2, 19, etc.

Sakhi, ‘friend,’ is common from the Rigveda^1 onwards,^2
both literally and metaphorically.
1) i. 164, 20 (of birds); iii. 43, 4 (of
steeds); ii. 1, 9; v. 12, 5; vi. 75, 3,
etc.
2) Av. v. 4, 7; 11, 9; 13, 5, etc. So
sakhitva and sakhya, ‘friendship,’ are
also common — e.g., Rv. i. 10, 6; iii. 1,
15; iv. 25, 2, etc., and Rv. 1. 178, 2;
ii. 18, 8; vii. 22, 9, etc.
